_comment: SYNTHETIC workshop data. Each scenario is a TIMELESS security-knowledge (SK) probe described in prose with NO CVE number, crossed with the LatamPay (CK) environment. archetype = hit | miss | sk_gated. expected_rubric is the ground truth the side-by-side panels are scored against: a=correct CWE (SK), b=used customer context (CK), c=correct prioritization/action (SK+CK). Customer Knowledge (asset applicability, SLA, tier) must come ONLY from the RAG customer pack, never from the model or the probe text.

scenarios.probe: A Java web application built on a framework that evaluates OGNL expressions takes a request parameter and passes it into a server-side expression that is then evaluated. An attacker can submit a crafted expression that the server executes.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Apache Struts web framework
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (Apache Struts 2.5.33, internet-facing, tier-0, PCI)
scenarios.expected_action: 24h SLA (internet-facing/tier-0); page security on-call, open Sev-1, document PCI compensating control within 4h.
scenarios.notes: Clean Hit: weakness lives in software LatamPay runs on its crown-jewel asset.

scenarios.probe: A logging library performs a lookup on attacker-influenced log message content and resolves a remote JNDI reference, loading and executing a remote object.
scenarios.weakness_name: Expression/Lookup Injection leading to remote code execution (Log4Shell-class)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Log4j logging library (log4j-core)
scenarios.ck_match: NONE — Log4j was removed fleet-wide in 2022 (INC-2022-0417); LatamPay uses Logback.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable and close with a note: Log4j is not present in the estate (removed 2022).
scenarios.notes: Miss: model should still recognize the weakness class, but CK says the affected component is absent.

scenarios.probe: An internal service reads a byte stream from a message queue and reconstructs application objects directly from it without validating the type or contents before reconstruction. The data originates from an upstream producer.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Java service that deserializes objects from a queue
scenarios.ck_match: reconciliation-service (internal, tier-1, deserializes Java objects from the settlement queue; flagged known-fragile)
scenarios.expected_action: Internal 30-day SLA (tier-1); add to remediation; note historical fragility from prior reviews.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: a shallow model may call this 'input validation' (e.g., CWE-20) or guess injection; only a security-deep model names CWE-502. CK then scopes it to internal.

scenarios.probe: A file-download endpoint builds a filesystem path by concatenating a user-supplied filename without normalizing it, allowing sequences like ../ to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internal document upload/download service
scenarios.ck_match: document-service (internal, tier-1, stores customer KYC documents / PII)
scenarios.expected_action: Internal 30-day SLA but escalate to Data Protection Officer because it exposes PII (KYC); treat as High minimum.
scenarios.notes: Hit with a CK twist: not internet-facing, but data classification raises the priority.

scenarios.probe: A notification webhook service accepts a merchant-supplied callback URL and makes an outbound HTTP request to it server-side, without restricting the destination, so an attacker can make the server request internal addresses.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Notification/webhook service that fetches merchant-supplied URLs
scenarios.ck_match: notification-service (Cloud VPC; outbound webhooks to merchant URLs; cloud metadata endpoint reachable)
scenarios.expected_action: Escalate: blast radius includes the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) → potential credential theft; prioritize above a generic internal finding.
scenarios.notes: Hit where CK (network zone note) drives the high severity via cloud-metadata reachability.

scenarios.probe: An internal admin tool builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating a value typed into a form, so an attacker can alter the filter logic with characters like ) and *.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internal admin tool querying a directory service
scenarios.ck_match: corporate-directory (LDAP/AD; internal admin tool builds filters from form input; Corp zone, tier-2)
scenarios.expected_action: Internal 30-day SLA (tier-2, internal-only); fix by parameterizing/escaping the LDAP filter.
scenarios.notes: Hit on an internal tier-2 asset; CK keeps the priority moderate.

scenarios.probe: A content-management plugin builds a SQL query by inserting an unescaped request parameter into a MySQL statement, allowing the attacker to alter the query.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: A MySQL-backed CMS plugin (e.g., WordPress plugin)
scenarios.ck_match: NONE — LatamPay runs PostgreSQL only and has no WordPress/CMS or MySQL in the estate.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: the affected product (MySQL CMS plugin) is not in the estate.
scenarios.notes: Miss: model should correctly identify SQL injection (CWE-89) but CK rules it out by missing software.

scenarios.probe: Code checks that a file is safe to use (e.g., verifies a property of the file), and then in a separate later step opens and uses that same file by name. Between the check and the use, the referenced file can be swapped.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internal service performing file check-then-use
scenarios.ck_match: document-service (internal, tier-1, handles files)
scenarios.expected_action: Internal 30-day SLA; fix by using atomic file-handle operations instead of name-based recheck.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: a shallow model often mislabels this as generic 'race condition' or path traversal; only a security-deep model names CWE-367 TOCTOU.

scenarios.probe: An internal reconciliation service exposes an administrative API endpoint that performs a sensitive action but does not require any authentication; anyone able to reach the endpoint can invoke it.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Admin endpoint on an internal reconciliation service
scenarios.ck_match: reconciliation-service admin endpoint (internal, tier-1, money-movement reconciliation)
scenarios.expected_action: Internal 30-day SLA, High due to money-movement sensitivity; add authentication/authorization.
scenarios.notes: Hit; CK (tier-1, reconciliation) raises severity.

scenarios.probe: An XML parser resolves external entities defined in the document, so a crafted document can reference and disclose local files or reach internal systems.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: A SOAP/XML gateway that parses XML
scenarios.ck_match: NONE — the legacy SOAP/XML gateway was decommissioned in 2024 (INC-2024-0631); no XML SOAP endpoints remain.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: the affected XML-parsing product was decommissioned in 2024.
scenarios.notes: Miss driven by incident history (decommission), not just the SBOM.

scenarios.probe: A payment gateway service ships with a database password written directly into a configuration file committed to the source repository, so anyone with repo access obtains the credential.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Payment gateway service configuration with embedded credentials
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI scope)
scenarios.expected_action: Tier-0/PCI → 24h SLA, Sev-1, rotate credential immediately, document PCI compensating control within 4h.
scenarios.notes: Hit; CK (tier-0/PCI) forces top priority.

scenarios.probe: A login flow takes a 'returnUrl' parameter and, after authentication, redirects the browser to that URL without validating that it points to an allowed site, so it can send users to an attacker-controlled domain.
scenarios.weakness_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internet-facing portal login flow
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1)
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing so prioritized above an internal equivalent, but lower severity than RCE-class; fix with an allowlist of redirect targets.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: shallow models frequently mislabel this as XSS (CWE-79) or phishing; only a security-deep model names CWE-601 Open Redirect.

scenarios.probe: A payment-gateway endpoint builds a SQL query by concatenating an unescaped request parameter directly into the statement sent to its relational database, so an attacker can alter the query and read or modify data.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Payment-gateway data-access layer over a relational database
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI, internet-facing) backed by PostgreSQL 14 — a relational DB IS in the estate, unlike the MySQL/CMS case.
scenarios.expected_action: Tier-0/PCI -> 24h SLA, Sev-1; parameterize queries; document PCI compensating control within 4h.
scenarios.notes: Hit contrast to S07: same CWE-89, but here the DB (PostgreSQL) IS in the estate, so it is applicable and tier-0 Critical.

scenarios.probe: An internet-facing customer portal stores a value submitted by one user and later renders it into another user's page without encoding it, so injected script executes in the victim's browser.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internet-facing portal that renders user-supplied content
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1; React SPA + Spring Boot).
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing customer surface -> High; output-encode and apply a content security policy.
scenarios.notes: Hit on the internet-facing portal; CK keeps it High (customer session theft) but below tier-0 RCE.

scenarios.probe: A document service accepts uploaded files and stores them without validating the file type or contents, so an attacker can upload an executable or script-bearing file.
scenarios.weakness_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Service that accepts user file uploads
scenarios.ck_match: document-service (internal, tier-1; ingests customer KYC/PII documents).
scenarios.expected_action: Internal 30-day SLA but High: handles PII and upload-to-execute can lead to RCE; validate type, store outside webroot, scan.
scenarios.notes: Hit; CK (PII + upload surface) raises priority to High.

scenarios.probe: A portal API returns a record identified by a numeric id taken directly from the request, without checking that the record belongs to the authenticated user, so changing the id returns other customers' data.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internet-facing portal API keyed by a user-supplied identifier
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1; serves customer account data).
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing PII exposure -> High; enforce per-object ownership checks on every request.
scenarios.notes: Hit; internet-facing customer data access drives High.

scenarios.probe: A payment-gateway feature builds an operating-system command that includes an unsanitized request value and executes it in a shell, so an attacker can inject additional commands.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Payment-gateway feature that shells out with user input
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI, internet-facing; Apache Struts).
scenarios.expected_action: Tier-0/PCI RCE-class -> 24h SLA, Sev-1; replace shell calls with safe APIs; document PCI compensating control within 4h.
scenarios.notes: Hit; command execution on the crown-jewel asset -> Critical.

scenarios.probe: A service stores sensitive personal identity documents on disk in plaintext, with no encryption at rest, so anyone who reaches the storage can read them.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Storage layer for sensitive documents
scenarios.ck_match: document-service (internal, tier-1; stores KYC/PII documents).
scenarios.expected_action: PII at rest -> escalate to Data Protection Officer, High; enable encryption at rest and tighten access.
scenarios.notes: Hit; data classification (KYC/PII) drives High even though internal.

scenarios.probe: A portal login accepts an authentication assertion but fails to properly verify it, allowing a crafted request to be accepted as an authenticated user.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internet-facing portal authentication flow
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1; customer authentication).
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing account takeover -> High; fix verification logic and add step-up/MFA where feasible.
scenarios.notes: Hit; distinct from S30 (signature-specific) and S09 (missing auth entirely).

scenarios.probe: A payment-gateway endpoint allocates work proportional to attacker-controlled input with no limit, so a small request can consume excessive CPU or memory and degrade service.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Payment-gateway endpoint without resource limits
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI, internet-facing).
scenarios.expected_action: Availability impact on tier-0 (not data/RCE) -> High; add input bounds, rate limiting, and timeouts.
scenarios.notes: Hit; availability-only impact keeps it High rather than Critical despite tier-0.

scenarios.probe: An internal service keeps the credentials it uses for downstream systems in a location readable by more users than necessary and without adequate protection, so they can be recovered by unauthorized parties.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internal service credential store
scenarios.ck_match: reconciliation-service (internal, tier-1; money-movement reconciliation).
scenarios.expected_action: Tier-1 money-movement -> High; move secrets to a managed vault, restrict access, and rotate.
scenarios.notes: Hit; distinct from S11 (hard-coded in source) - here it is weak protection of stored credentials.

scenarios.probe: A payment-gateway configuration file that contains sensitive settings is created with permissions that allow any local account to read and modify it.
scenarios.weakness_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Payment-gateway configuration file permissions
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI, internet-facing).
scenarios.expected_action: Tier-0/PCI sensitive config exposure -> 24h SLA, Sev-1; tighten file permissions and audit access.
scenarios.notes: Hit; tier-0/PCI config exposure -> Critical.

scenarios.probe: A .NET application deserializes attacker-controlled data using a legacy binary formatter, reconstructing arbitrary object graphs that can trigger code execution.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: .NET application using a legacy binary formatter
scenarios.ck_match: NONE - LatamPay runs a Java/Spring stack; there is no .NET application in the estate.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: the affected platform (.NET) is not in the estate.
scenarios.notes: Miss: correct weakness (CWE-502) but wrong platform; contrast S03 (Java deserialization, applicable).

scenarios.probe: A PHP application includes a file whose path is taken from a request parameter, allowing an attacker to cause a remote or unintended file to be included and executed.
scenarios.weakness_name: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require (PHP Remote File Inclusion)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: PHP/CMS application (e.g., a WordPress plugin)
scenarios.ck_match: NONE - LatamPay runs no PHP, WordPress, or CMS in the estate.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: no PHP/CMS/WordPress software is present.
scenarios.notes: Miss: PHP-specific weakness; no PHP stack in the estate.

scenarios.probe: An application builds a database query object from unsanitized request fields for a document database, letting an attacker inject operators that alter the query logic.
scenarios.weakness_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Application backed by a NoSQL/document database (e.g., MongoDB)
scenarios.ck_match: NONE - LatamPay uses PostgreSQL 14 (relational) only; no MongoDB or NoSQL store is in the estate.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: no NoSQL/document database is present.
scenarios.notes: Miss: correct injection class but the datastore (MongoDB) is absent; contrast S13 (SQLi on PostgreSQL, applicable).

scenarios.probe: A server-side JavaScript service merges attacker-controlled JSON into objects in a way that lets special property names alter the object prototype, changing application behavior.
scenarios.weakness_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes (Prototype Pollution)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Node.js server-side service performing recursive object merge
scenarios.ck_match: NONE - the portal backend is Spring Boot (Java); LatamPay runs no Node.js server-side service.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: no Node.js backend is present (backend is Java/Spring).
scenarios.notes: Miss: React is frontend only; the server-side Node runtime this needs is not in the estate.

scenarios.probe: A Ruby on Rails controller assigns request parameters directly to model attributes without allow-listing, so an attacker can set fields that were never meant to be user-writable.
scenarios.weakness_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes (Mass Assignment)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Ruby on Rails application binding request params to model attributes
scenarios.ck_match: NONE - LatamPay runs a Java/Spring stack; there is no Ruby on Rails application in the estate.
scenarios.expected_action: Mark Not Applicable: no Ruby on Rails application is present.
scenarios.notes: Miss: framework-specific weakness on a stack the estate does not run.

scenarios.probe: An internal service performs an authorization check but evaluates the wrong attribute, so a low-privilege authenticated user can act on records belonging to others.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internal service with a flawed authorization decision
scenarios.ck_match: reconciliation-service (internal, tier-1; money-movement reconciliation).
scenarios.expected_action: Tier-1 money-movement -> High; correct the authorization predicate and add tests.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: shallow models say generic 'broken access control' or 'missing authentication' (CWE-306); the precise weakness is CWE-863 incorrect (not missing) authorization.

scenarios.probe: A portal accepts a session identifier supplied before login and continues to use that same identifier after the user authenticates, so an attacker who planted the identifier can ride the authenticated session.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Internet-facing portal session management
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1; authenticated customer sessions).
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing session hijack -> High; regenerate the session identifier on authentication.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: shallow models call this a generic 'session management' or 'authentication' issue; the precise weakness is CWE-384 session fixation.

scenarios.probe: An internet-facing portal accepts JSON Web Tokens and, when a token declares its algorithm as 'none', treats it as valid without verifying any signature, so an attacker can forge tokens with arbitrary claims.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Portal authentication layer validating JWTs
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1) - handles authenticated customer sessions.
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing account-takeover risk -> High; reject 'none'/unexpected algorithms and verify signatures against pinned keys.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: shallow models call this generic 'authentication bypass' (CWE-287); the precise weakness is CWE-347 signature-verification failure.

scenarios.probe: A payment-gateway input validator uses a regular expression whose matching time grows explosively on certain inputs, so a crafted string makes a single request consume large amounts of CPU.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Input validation using a catastrophically backtracking regular expression
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI, internet-facing).
scenarios.expected_action: Availability impact on tier-0 (not data/RCE) -> High; replace the regex with a linear-time matcher and add input caps.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: shallow models label this generic 'denial of service' (CWE-400); the precise weakness is CWE-1333 regex complexity (ReDoS).

scenarios.probe: A portal generates password-reset tokens using a general-purpose random number generator that is not cryptographically secure, so tokens can be predicted by an attacker.
scenarios.weakness_name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Portal token generation using a non-cryptographic PRNG
scenarios.ck_match: customer-portal (internet-facing, tier-1; password-reset flow).
scenarios.expected_action: Internet-facing account takeover via predictable tokens -> High; use a cryptographically secure RNG.
scenarios.notes: SK-gated: shallow models say generic 'weak cryptography' or 'insecure randomness'; the precise weakness is CWE-338 weak PRNG.
